findings.summary: FinCEN issued a consent order against TD Bank, N.A. and TD Bank USA, N.A. imposing a $1.3 billion civil money penalty for Bank Secrecy Act violations; the bank will pay $757 million to the U.S. Treasury.
The OCC issued a cease‑and‑desist order and a $450 million civil money penalty, along with a growth restriction and asset cap, for BSA/AML deficiencies at TD Bank, N.A. and TD Bank USA, N.A.
The CFTC ordered TD Bank to pay a $75 million civil monetary penalty for recordkeeping and supervision failures related to the use of unapproved communication methods.
The CFTC ordered TD Bank to pay a $4 million civil monetary penalty for supervision failures affecting its electronic communications surveillance system.
The CFPB ordered TD Bank to pay a $20 million civil money penalty and $7.76 million in redress to consumers for illegal credit‑reporting practices.
The Federal Reserve Board fined TD Bank $123.5 million for anti‑money‑laundering violations and required remedial actions.
TD Bank, N.A. entered a guilty plea to a criminal violation of 18 U.S.C. §371 (conspiracy) in coordination with the DOJ, as part of a broader settlement package.

A New Jersey federal judge dismissed the proposed nationwide class action alleging TD Bank shared customers' personal financial information via a hidden Meta tracking pixel, granting TD Bank’s motion to dismiss.

The Ontario Superior Court of Justice certified a class‑action lawsuit against TD Bank and senior leaders for alleged misrepresentations about the bank’s anti‑money‑laundering controls and related investigations.
U.S. District Court in New Jersey gave final approval to the $32,225,000 Burns overdraft‑fee settlement against TD Bank.
Payments under the Burns overdraft‑fee settlement to former TD Bank customers began in March 2025.
The Trisal overdraft‑fee class action against TD Bank was terminated by the court on May 15, 2026.
The Ontario Superior Court approved a settlement of the TD Bank Duplicative NSF Fees class action on February 15, 2024.

U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York partially denied TD Bank’s motion to dismiss the securities‑fraud class action Tiessen v. TD Bank on October 13, 2026, allowing the case to proceed to discovery.
Plaintiffs filed a Third Amended Complaint in the TD Bank / First Horizon securities litigation on January 31, 2025.
A proposed class‑action lawsuit alleging TD Bank and TD Securities failed to pay vacation and holiday pay on incentive compensation was filed in the Ontario Superior Court on July 8, 2026.
The complaint initiating the Trisal overdraft‑fee class action against TD Bank was filed on October 2, 2025.

TD Bank and its parent company pleaded guilty in October 2024 to Bank Secrecy Act violations and money‑laundering conspiracy, agreeing to pay $1.8 billion in penalties, the largest BSA penalty ever imposed.
FinCEN assessed a record $1.3 billion civil penalty against TD Bank in October 2024 for failing to limit, report, and monitor suspicious transactions and cash activity linked to criminal activity.
Former TD Bank employee Gerardo Aquino pleaded guilty in October 2026 to accepting bribes and laundering more than $4.8 million to Colombia.

Former TD Bank employee Wilfredo Aquino pleaded guilty in January 2026 to conspiring to launder monetary instruments, facilitating a scheme that moved approximately $474 million through TD Bank accounts.
Former TD Bank employee Nunez pleaded guilty in January 2026 to accepting bribes and facilitating a Colombian ATM money‑laundering scheme that moved over $26 million out of the United States.
Former TD Bank employee Leonardo Ayala pleaded guilty in January 2026 to accepting bribes and laundering approximately $5.5 million to Colombia through fraudulent accounts and debit cards.
TD Bank, N.A. settled with OFAC for apparent violations of the North Korea Sanctions Regulations and the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations, paying a $115,005.04 civil penalty.
TD Bank was indicted for knowingly failing to maintain an adequate anti‑money‑laundering program, including violations of U.S. sanctions, for conduct spanning 2014‑2023.
A couple's TD Bank accounts were targeted by thieves after a ransomware incident on their home computer, resulting in unauthorized transfers; TD Bank denied the refund request.
NCB Management Services suffered a data breach that exposed over a million records, including personal and financial information of TD Bank customers.
TD Bank disclosed an insider data breach where a former employee accessed customer information between August and December 2022; the breach was reported in February 2025.

TD Bank confirmed an insider data breach affecting U.S. customers, with unauthorized employee access to names, SSNs, account numbers and transaction data from January 7 to January 30, 2026; the breach was reported in June 2026 and TD offered additional safeguards.
A whistleblower alleged that senior management at TD Bank ignored warning signs and failed to address compliance gaps, contributing to a government settlement involving a multi‑billion‑dollar fine.

Senator Elizabeth Warren’s letter to the DOJ accused TD Bank executives of presiding over a criminally deficient anti‑money‑laundering program and facilitating illicit activity, citing a proposed $3 billion fine and suggesting leadership failures.
